title: Growing something green
description: Herbs on a windowsill teach patience, seasons, and where food comes from — for pennies.

body.heading: Start with herbs
paragraphs: You do not need a garden to grow food. Basil, mint, coriander, and spring onions grow happily in pots on a sunny windowsill, and herbs are among the most expensive supermarket items per gram — so homegrown ones genuinely save money.
Seeds cost very little, and some plants regrow from kitchen scraps: spring onion roots in a glass of water will sprout fresh greens more than once.

body.heading: Care is the curriculum
paragraphs: A plant teaches a daily rhythm: light, water, patience, and noticing small changes. For young people especially, growing something is a calm counterweight to instant everything.
Failures are part of it. A wilted pot is a lesson about water or light, not a verdict on you as a gardener. Try again with what you learned.

body.heading: Share the harvest
paragraphs: A handful of homegrown herbs given to a neighbour or stirred into a shared meal turns a small pot into a small kindness — which is rather the point of SparkKindly.

takeaway: Grow herbs on a windowsill: cheap, calming, and quietly educational.
